notes.title: How an 88% S3 cut actually happens
notes.excerpt: Most S3 bills are forgotten storage classes, not request volume.
notes.body: Object storage gets expensive when every backup stays in Standard forever. The cut came from two boring controls: lifecycle rules that move cold objects into cheaper classes, and compressing backup artifacts before they land in the bucket. The important part is measuring the bill per prefix first. Without that, lifecycle policies become guesswork and you risk moving data that still needs millisecond reads.

notes.title: Why Harbor replaced ECR here
notes.excerpt: Managed registries are convenient until image retention becomes a line item.
notes.body: ECR is fine until retention, replication, and vulnerability scanning stack on top of compute you already pay for elsewhere. Harbor on Hetzner kept scanning in GitHub Actions, gave a self-hosted registry that the cluster already trusted, and dropped about 60% of registry spend. The migration path that mattered was tag immutability plus a dual-pull window so Swarm services never raced a registry cutover.

notes.title: Databases should not have a public story
notes.excerpt: A security group with your office IP is not a zero-trust design.
notes.body: The production database now accepts traffic only from the WireGuard interface. Operators join the mesh, then use the internal address. That removes the 'just allow 5432 from this CIDR' exception that always grows. Rotate peer keys, keep split-tunneling limited to the data subnet, and log handshake failures the same way you log SSH.

notes.title: Traces before more dashboards
notes.excerpt: Another Grafana row will not explain a slow checkout.
notes.body: Metrics say something is wrong. Traces say which hop. SigNoz on OpenTelemetry let Node services emit spans without a vendor SDK lock-in, while Prometheus still scraped platform metrics. Alertmanager stayed the pager. The rule I keep: no new dashboard until the service emits a useful trace id in its error logs.

notes.title: Canaries need a flag, not a prayer
notes.excerpt: Shipping 100% of traffic on a Friday is a habit, not a strategy.
notes.body: Unleash sits in front of risky behavior so a bad build does not require a full rollback to hide a feature. Combine that with a canary ReplicaSet or weighted service and you get two independent kill switches: traffic weight and flag state. That is the difference between a deploy and a release.
